figures.alt: A phone with no cell signal sends a text up to a satellite, which passes it down to a ground station.

figures.caption: **Figure 1. One text, up and back down.** The green legs are the trip through the air: the slow, fragile part. Not to scale.
figures.alt: A normal text goes from your phone to a nearby tower. A satellite text goes up to a satellite and back down to a ground station first.

figures.caption: **Figure 2. A long way for a faint signal.** The message goes up in small pieces, one after another. Not to scale.
figures.alt: A text travels from a phone with a tiny antenna to a satellite hundreds of miles away, sent a few words at a time.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. What's between you and the sky.** Open sky is best. Trees slow it down. Buildings and canyons can stop it.
figures.alt: Open sky works in about 30 seconds. Under trees it is slower. In a canyon or indoors it may not connect.

figures.caption: **Figure 4. The sky from where you stand.** Many satellites move across the sky. When one drops behind a hill, your phone waits for the next one. Not to scale.
figures.alt: Satellites move across the sky. You can reach one high overhead or low near the horizon, but not one hidden behind a hill.

figures.caption: **Figure 5. Hold it out in the open.** Left: what to do. Right: what loses the satellite.
figures.alt: Do: hold the phone in your hand outdoors and follow the arrow. Don't: leave it in a pocket or pack, or walk under trees.

figures.caption: **Figure 6. Text first.** Left: what can go by satellite. Right: what waits.
figures.alt: Short texts and, on some phones, your location go by satellite. Photos, video and calls wait for coverage.

figures.caption: **Figure 7. A backup, not a promise.** All four have to line up at once. Your plan with someone at home is the part that doesn't depend on the sky.
figures.alt: Satellite texting needs open sky, a phone that has it, a charged battery and time. So leave your route and return time with someone at home.

figures.caption: **Figure 8. Do it all before you lose signal.** The numbers match the steps below.
figures.alt: Six things to do at home while you still have a signal. Out of signal, all that is left is sending the text.
